title: Shut-down fixedTimeLimit executor: RejectedExecutionException from submit is recorded as the callable's failure though the callable never ran
cause: Retryer.call wraps every Throwable from attemptTimeLimiter.call in an ExceptionAttempt numbered as the current attempt (Retryer.java:162-163). With fixedTimeLimit(d, unit, executor), Guava 22.0 SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout calls executor.submit (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:149) outside its try block, so a shut-down executor's RejectedExecutionException reaches that catch. Retryer.call records it as an exception the callable threw, although the callable was never submitted or run.
trigger: The ExecutorService passed to AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit(d, unit, executor) is shut down (shutdown() or shutdownNow(), on a cached, fixed, single-thread or ForkJoin pool) before Retryer.call, or while call() is waiting between attempts. Then the next attempt's submit is rejected.
consequence: With a predicate that does not match RejectedExecutionException (e.g. retryIfExceptionOfType(IOException)), call() throws ExecutionException(RejectedExecutionException), which its Javadoc reserves for 'the given callable throws an exception'. The callable was invoked 0 times, yet listeners are notified of attempt #1 with hasException()=true. With retryIfException()/retryIfRuntimeException(), each rejection is retried as a callable failure. stopAfterAttempt(3) gives a RetryException reporting 3 failed attempts and 0 invocations. The defaults neverStop+noWait busy-loop at about 100% CPU (about 130k-280k fabricated attempts per second across four runs). The README exponential-backoff configuration (neverStop) never returns. In every case the callable is never invoked.
premises: The time limiter comes from the public 3-argument AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit(duration, unit, executorService) with a caller-supplied executor that is shut down before or during Retryer.call. Users cannot shut down the internal cached pool of the 2-argument overload.

Guava 22.0 (jar sha1 3564ef3803de51fb0530a8377ec6100b33b0d073) SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout(callable, d, unit, true) calls executor.submit at line 149 before its try block, so the executor's RejectedExecutionException propagates unwrapped to Retryer.call.

No library or caller-side guard distinguishes limiter/executor failures from callable failures. The documented contract of Retryer.call, Attempt and RetryException describes attempts and ExecutionException causes as the callable's own outcome.

Distinct from upstream #29 (timeouts not retried): #29 concerns UncheckedTimeoutException from future.get after the callable was submitted. Its proposed fix (TimeoutException vs ExecutionException from the limiter) would not cover a raw RejectedExecutionException from submit.

Reproduced at escalation level 0 on JDK 21 (--release 8) against unmodified source 177b6c9b9f3e7957f404f0bdb8e23374cb1de43f. Results were deterministic in four runs: two in round 0 and two in repair round 1 on 2026-11-26, each with 7/7 scenario checks triggered.

Repair round 1 regenerated the counterexamples on the repaired spec (spec/output/repair-r1/repair1_s4_shutdown_bfs2.out, spec/output/repair-r1/repair1_ctl_s4_shutdown_cir.out). The action sequence and violated invariants are unchanged; only curQueued after MCSubmitRejected changed from TRUE to FALSE. FALSE matches the implementation: a shut-down ThreadPoolExecutor rejects without enqueueing, and the repro observes taskCount=0, queue.size=0 and largestPoolSize=0 during onRetry.
